brief: William Wilberforce was born in 1759 and, after studies at Cambridge, entered Parliament in 1780. He was converted to evangelical Christianity in 1784 and became an important spokesman for evangelical ideas. He promoted education, missions and moral reform. The trade in slaves soon drew his attention, and he attacked slavery and the slave trade vigorously. Acts of Parliament in 1807 finally abolished the trade in slaves. It was not until 1833, a month after Wilberforce’s death, that the Emancipation Act freed slaves in all British territories. Wilberforce was buried in Westminster Abbey.
